name: Health & Wellness
description: A holistic course exploring the multiple dimensions of wellness — physical, mental, emotional, social, and environmental — and strategies for creating a balanced, healthy lifestyle.

modules.title: Dimensions of Wellness
modules.objectives: Identify the eight dimensions of wellness (emotional, financial, social, spiritual, occupational, physical, intellectual, and environmental) and explain how they interconnect.
modules.readingNote: SAMHSA — Creating a Healthier Life; use the official step-by-step guide to the eight dimensions of wellness for the wellness-wheel analysis.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 1: Dimensions of Wellness lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Use the SAMHSA eight-dimension guide to classify the fictional examples in the module; no personal health, financial, trauma, or diagnostic disclosure is required.
modules.assignment: Submit: a completed eight-dimension wellness wheel for a fictional or generalized student plus a one-page reflection. Include: ratings for all eight dimensions, two evidence-based growth areas, and one realistic action for each; personal observations may be anonymized, and diagnoses, financial details, trauma, or other sensitive information are not required. Evaluation: the wheel is complete, the reflection uses evidence from the module, and each action clearly connects to a named dimension.

modules.title: Physical Wellness & Exercise
modules.objectives: Explain how regular physical activity contributes to overall wellness, understand physical activity guidelines for adolescents, and identify barriers to exercise.
modules.readingNote: CDC — Child Activity: An Overview; use the age 6–17 aerobic, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening recommendations.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 2: Physical Wellness & Exercise lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the CDC age 6–17 guidance to the same fictional two-week activity log used in the assignment; identify one gradual, enjoyable adjustment.
modules.assignment: Submit: a two-week activity log based on provided sample data, a fictional profile, or anonymized personal data. Include: activity type, duration, intensity, two evidence-based mood or energy patterns, and one realistic adjustment; medical diagnoses are not required. Evaluation: the log is complete, the two patterns are supported by entries, and the adjustment connects to adolescent activity guidance.

modules.title: Nutritional Wellness
modules.objectives: Use current federal dietary guidance to evaluate balanced, nutrient-dense food choices and explain how nutrition and hydration can affect energy, mood, growth, and long-term health.
modules.readingNote: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — current Dietary Guidelines for Americans and supporting resources.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 3: Nutritional Wellness lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Submit: an annotated three-day food log and short reflection using provided, fictional, or anonymized data. Include: two strengths, two realistic improvements, and citations to current federal dietary guidance; calories, weight, diagnoses, and sensitive health details are not required. Evaluation: the analysis uses specific log evidence and accurately connects food variety, nutrient density, or hydration to the module objective.

modules.title: Mental & Emotional Health
modules.objectives: Define mental and emotional health, identify common mental health conditions in adolescents, and describe strategies for maintaining positive mental health.
modules.readingNote: NIMH — Child and Adolescent Mental Health; distinguish ordinary variation from persistent warning signs and review when evaluation or urgent help may be appropriate.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 4: Mental & Emotional Health lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the NIMH warning-sign and help-seeking guidance to a fictional student scenario; this is not a self-screen, diagnosis, or request for personal disclosure.
modules.assignment: Submit: a one-page guide to two evidence-based mental-health strategies for adolescents. Include: a qualified source for each strategy, steps for safe practice, limits of self-help, and when a trusted adult or health professional should be contacted. Evaluation: each recommendation is supported by evidence, is feasible for a teenager, and avoids diagnosis or promises of a cure.

modules.title: Stress Management
modules.objectives: Identify common stressors for teenagers, explain the physiological stress response, and apply multiple evidence-based stress management techniques. Students will connect concepts to safe practice, explain risks or benefits, and document evidence of understanding in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: APA — Stress Management Tips — for background reading on Stress Management before the quiz and assignment
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 5: Stress Management lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Apply one evidence-based coping strategy to a fictional school-stress scenario for five days of sample entries; do not disclose trauma or private mental-health history.
modules.assignment: Submit: a stress-management toolkit for a fictional student or generalized school-stress scenario. Include: three stressors, one evidence-based coping strategy for each, and an explanation of when trusted-adult or professional support is appropriate; trauma and private mental-health history are not required. Evaluation: each strategy fits its stressor, uses course evidence, and includes a safe support threshold.

modules.title: Sleep & Recovery
modules.objectives: Explain the stages of sleep, understand the recommended sleep duration for teenagers, and identify habits that promote and disrupt healthy sleep.
modules.readingNote: CDC — Sleep and Health; use the age-based sleep recommendations and school-focused evidence on sleep, concentration, and health.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 6: Sleep & Recovery lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: NHLBI — How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages. NREM includes stages 1–3, with stage 3 called deep or slow-wave sleep; REM usually includes vivid dreaming and muscle atonia (temporarily reduced muscle tone). Use this overview, then analyze this fictional five-night log against the CDC teen sleep range: Mon 11:45 p.m.–6:30 a.m. (6 h 45 min; phone used after lights-out), Tue 11:30 p.m.–6:30 a.m. (7 h), Wed 12:15 a.m.–6:30 a.m. (6 h 15 min; caffeinated drink at 7 p.m.), Thu 10:45 p.m.–6:30 a.m. (7 h 45 min), Fri 12:30 a.m.–8:30 a.m. (8 h). Do not diagnose a sleep disorder.
modules.assignment: Submit: a five-night sleep analysis and a realistic two-week improvement plan using the fictional log in the practice note, or an equivalent fictional or anonymized log with bed time, wake time, estimated duration, and relevant routine notes. Include: duration calculations, an accurate NREM/REM comparison and whole-night recovery context (no single stage alone explains recovery), three patterns, and three specific adjustments; diagnoses and sensitive details are not required. Evaluation: the calculations are traceable, each pattern is supported by specific log evidence, and the plan uses source evidence to connect those patterns to CDC adolescent sleep guidance and the NHLBI Sleep Phases and Stages resource.

modules.title: Social Health & Relationships
modules.objectives: Define social health, identify characteristics of healthy vs. unhealthy relationships, and understand effective communication skills for building positive connections.
modules.readingNote: CDC — Teen Dating Violence; review healthy communication, unsafe behaviors, prevention, and support resources without requiring personal relationship disclosure.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 7: Social Health & Relationships lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Classify the behaviors in a fictional peer or dating scenario as healthy, unhealthy, or unsafe, then name one boundary and one support option.
modules.assignment: Submit: a written analysis of a provided or fictional friendship or family scenario. Include: healthy qualities, warning signs, boundaries, and one communication skill that could improve the interaction; personal relationship disclosure is not required. Evaluation: claims cite scenario evidence and correctly apply relationship-safety and communication concepts.

modules.title: Substance Use & Prevention
modules.objectives: Identify the short- and long-term health effects of tobacco, alcohol, and other substances on the developing brain, and apply refusal skills and protective strategies.
modules.readingNote: CDC — About Underage Drinking; use the current youth-risk evidence and distinguish association from causation.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 8: Substance Use & Prevention lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: Use NIDA prevention guidance to identify two risk factors, two protective factors, and three refusal or exit strategies for a fictional peer-pressure scenario.
modules.assignment: Submit: a peer-facing prevention resource about alcohol, nicotine, or cannabis. Include: accurate developing-brain effects, at least two risk and two protective factors, three refusal or exit strategies, and two qualified support sources. Evaluation: the resource is accurate, non-stigmatizing, useful in a real peer-pressure scenario, and clearly connects each strategy to course evidence.

quizQuestions.question: How many dimensions of wellness does SAMHSA identify?
quizQuestions.explanation: SAMHSA identifies 8 dimensions of wellness: emotional, financial, social, spiritual, occupational, physical, intellectual, and environmental.

quizQuestions.question: Which best describes the concept of 'holistic wellness'?
options: Giving physical fitness priority over the other dimensions
Considering connections and shifting priorities
Giving each dimension equal time regardless of circumstances
Measuring wellness mainly through the absence of illness
quizQuestions.answer: Considering connections and shifting priorities
quizQuestions.explanation: A whole-person approach considers how dimensions influence one another without assuming every dimension has the same priority for every person or situation.

quizQuestions.question: Which example best shows that wellness dimensions are interconnected?
options: A student reads a novel for intellectual enjoyment
A student practices stretches to improve physical flexibility
Financial strain disrupts a student’s sleep and concentration
A student joins a club to build social connections
quizQuestions.answer: Financial strain disrupts a student’s sleep and concentration
quizQuestions.explanation: Financial strain can affect emotional, physical, occupational, and intellectual wellness, showing that the dimensions influence one another.

quizQuestions.question: What does occupational wellness mean for a high school student?
quizQuestions.answer: Occupational wellness for a high school student means finding purpose, growth, balance, and satisfaction in school, responsibilities, skill-building, and future career preparation.
quizQuestions.explanation: A strong response connects present responsibilities and strengths with a sustainable future path; it does not require having a paid job.

quizQuestions.question: How much daily physical activity do adolescents need according to health guidelines?
options: 90 minutes per day
30 minutes per day
20 minutes per day
60 minutes per day
quizQuestions.answer: 60 minutes per day
quizQuestions.explanation: The CDC recommends that adolescents get at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity every day.

quizQuestions.question: Which activity category should teens include at least 3 days per week under CDC guidance?
options: Muscle-strengthening activities
Low-intensity walking activities
Gentle flexibility activities
Light balance-training activities
quizQuestions.answer: Muscle-strengthening activities
quizQuestions.explanation: Muscle and bone-strengthening activities (resistance training, gymnastics) are recommended at least 3 days per week for teens.

quizQuestions.question: Which barrier is most directly addressed by scheduling activity around homework and social plans?
options: Believing a gym membership is required for activity
Expecting activity to count only in organized sports
Fitting activity around school and social commitments
Assuming shorter activity periods cannot be useful
quizQuestions.answer: Fitting activity around school and social commitments
quizQuestions.explanation: Time constraints from school, homework, and social activities are among the most frequently cited barriers to teen physical activity.

quizQuestions.question: A student wants to build toward the daily activity guideline safely. Which plan is most appropriate?
options: Begin with demanding sessions and add recovery later
Save the weekly activity goal for one long session
Use the same workload even when pain develops
Build up gradually with enjoyable, varied activities
quizQuestions.answer: Build up gradually with enjoyable, varied activities
quizQuestions.explanation: A gradual, enjoyable plan supports consistency and lowers injury risk while working toward the daily guideline.

quizQuestions.question: Which meal pattern best reflects current federal guidance for nutrient-dense choices?
options: A meal of juice, refined cereal, and a sweetened bar
A meal of vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and beans
A meal of white bread, processed meat, and soda
A meal of chips, sweetened yogurt, and fruit punch
quizQuestions.answer: A meal of vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and beans
quizQuestions.explanation: Current guidance emphasizes varied nutrient-dense foods that support growth and health while reducing reliance on highly processed foods.

quizQuestions.question: How does poor nutrition most directly affect mental wellness?
options: Deficiencies can affect brain function and mood
Effects appear chiefly as changes in appearance
Mood changes mainly reflect the taste of food
Taking supplements reliably improves mental health
quizQuestions.answer: Deficiencies can affect brain function and mood
quizQuestions.explanation: Adequate nutrition supports brain function. Deficiencies can affect attention, energy, and mood, but mental health has many influences; supplements are not a substitute for appropriate support.

quizQuestions.question: Which eating habit best supports nutritional wellness?
options: Choosing convenience foods mainly for their health claims
Choosing varied nutrient-dense foods across food groups
Selecting foods chiefly by the lowest calorie count
Relying on a supplement to make a limited diet balanced
quizQuestions.answer: Choosing varied nutrient-dense foods across food groups
quizQuestions.explanation: Nutritional wellness is supported by variety, balance, and adequacy — choosing whole foods from all food groups in appropriate amounts.

quizQuestions.question: How can hydration affect a student's daily wellness?
quizQuestions.answer: Adequate hydration supports temperature regulation, circulation, concentration, mood, and physical performance; needs vary with activity, climate, body size, diet, and health.
quizQuestions.explanation: A strong response links hydration to both body function and school or activity performance without claiming one fixed intake fits everyone.

quizQuestions.question: Mental health is best defined as:
options: Emotional, psychological, and social well-being
The absence of a diagnosed mental-health condition
Academic performance and measured intellectual ability
An ability to remain calm when daily demands increase
quizQuestions.answer: Emotional, psychological, and social well-being
quizQuestions.explanation: Mental health encompasses emotional, psychological, and social well-being, affecting how we think, feel, and interact with the world.

quizQuestions.question: A student has persistent anxiety that disrupts sleep and schoolwork. What is the safest next step?
options: Wait for the next school break before considering support
Tell a trusted adult and seek qualified professional help
Focus on study tips before mentioning the anxiety
Rely on reassurance from classmates without adult input
quizQuestions.answer: Tell a trusted adult and seek qualified professional help
quizQuestions.explanation: Persistent distress that interferes with daily life deserves support from a trusted adult and a qualified professional.

quizQuestions.question: Which is NOT a healthy coping strategy for mental health challenges?
options: Taking a walk to manage tension
Writing in a private journal
Talking with a trusted adult
Drinking alcohol to ease anxiety
quizQuestions.answer: Drinking alcohol to ease anxiety
quizQuestions.explanation: Alcohol is an unhealthy and potentially harmful coping mechanism that masks symptoms rather than addressing mental health challenges.

quizQuestions.question: Stigma around mental health prevents many teens from seeking help because:
options: They may confuse appointment costs with treatment quality
They may expect judgment or different treatment from others
They may be unsure how to schedule a first appointment
They may lack transport to an available support service
quizQuestions.answer: They may expect judgment or different treatment from others
quizQuestions.explanation: Fear of judgment, labeling, or social consequences can delay help-seeking; accurate information and supportive responses can reduce this barrier.

quizQuestions.question: Which pair represents the rapid sympathetic-adrenal stress response and the slower HPA-axis response, respectively?
options: Insulin and glucagon
Melatonin and thyroxine
Epinephrine and cortisol
Estrogen and progesterone
quizQuestions.answer: Epinephrine and cortisol
quizQuestions.explanation: Adrenaline supports the rapid sympathetic response, while cortisol is part of the slower hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal response; their timing and effects are not identical.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is an evidence-based stress management technique?
options: Practicing slow breathing and mindful attention
Repeatedly checking the same unfinished task list
Postponing a solvable problem without a plan
Seeking repeated reassurance without taking action
quizQuestions.answer: Practicing slow breathing and mindful attention
quizQuestions.explanation: Slow breathing and mindfulness can help regulate stress responses. They are coping tools, and persistent distress or impaired functioning still calls for appropriate support.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement best distinguishes acute stress from chronic stress?
options: Acute stress is physical; chronic stress is emotional
Acute stress is harmful; chronic stress is motivating
Acute stress is brief; chronic stress persists or recurs
Acute stress is voluntary; chronic stress is involuntary
quizQuestions.answer: Acute stress is brief; chronic stress persists or recurs
quizQuestions.explanation: Duration and repetition help distinguish an immediate stress response from ongoing stress that can strain health.

quizQuestions.question: When stress-management strategies are not enough and daily functioning is worsening, what should a teen do?
options: Keep trying the same technique before telling anyone
Reduce sleep to make more time for unfinished work
Rely on friends to handle the problem without adults
Seek trusted adult and qualified professional help
quizQuestions.answer: Seek trusted adult and qualified professional help
quizQuestions.explanation: Evidence-based self-management includes recognizing when additional support is needed, especially when stress persists or disrupts sleep, safety, relationships, or schoolwork.

quizQuestions.question: How many hours of sleep per night do teenagers need?
options: 6–7 hours
11–12 hours
5–6 hours
8–10 hours
quizQuestions.answer: 8–10 hours
quizQuestions.explanation: The CDC and American Academy of Sleep Medicine recommend 8–10 hours of sleep per night for teenagers aged 13–18.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement accurately describes typical REM sleep?
options: Muscles regularly move to act out vivid dreams
Brain activity falls to its lowest nightly level
Vivid dreams often occur with reduced muscle tone
REM is the deepest of the three NREM stages
quizQuestions.answer: Vivid dreams often occur with reduced muscle tone
quizQuestions.explanation: REM often includes vivid dreaming and muscle atonia, meaning most skeletal muscles become temporarily limp. NREM has stages 1–3; stage 3 is deep or slow-wave sleep. Healthy sleep includes cycling through NREM and REM, rather than one stage alone accounting for recovery.

quizQuestions.question: Blue light from screens before bed disrupts sleep by:
options: Suppressing melatonin and delaying sleep timing
Increasing melatonin as the eyes become tired
Advancing the body clock through mental alertness
Increasing sleep pressure by tiring the brain
quizQuestions.answer: Suppressing melatonin and delaying sleep timing
quizQuestions.explanation: Bright evening light, including blue light from screens, can suppress melatonin and delay circadian timing. Light intensity, timing, duration, and other aspects of screen use also matter.

quizQuestions.question: Which habit most directly supports a consistent sleep schedule?
options: Use screen time in bed to decide when to sleep
Shift bedtime later after each demanding school day
Keep similar sleep and wake times across the week
Use evening caffeine to complete work before bed
quizQuestions.answer: Keep similar sleep and wake times across the week
quizQuestions.explanation: A regular sleep-wake schedule helps align the body's circadian rhythm and makes adequate sleep more predictable across school days and weekends.

quizQuestions.question: Name two ways insufficient sleep can affect teenagers.
quizQuestions.answer: Insufficient sleep can impair attention, learning, mood regulation, reaction time, immune function, and safety; a strong answer accurately explains any two.
quizQuestions.explanation: Teen sleep loss can affect school performance, emotional well-being, physical health, and accident risk.

quizQuestions.question: A healthy relationship is characterized by:
options: Mutual respect, honesty, and support
Agreement maintained by avoiding difficult topics
Reassurance gained through checking private messages
Closeness maintained by limiting outside friendships
quizQuestions.answer: Mutual respect, honesty, and support
quizQuestions.explanation: Healthy relationships are built on mutual respect, trust, open communication, honesty, and support for each other's wellbeing.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a warning sign of an unhealthy relationship?
options: Discussing disagreements while respecting separate choices
Restricting a partner’s friendships and monitoring messages
Asking permission before sharing a partner’s personal story
Encouraging time with friends outside the relationship
quizQuestions.answer: Restricting a partner’s friendships and monitoring messages
quizQuestions.explanation: Controlling behavior, including monitoring movements, isolating from friends, or making decisions for the partner, is a warning sign of abuse.

quizQuestions.question: A friend says no to sharing a password. Which response best respects a healthy boundary?
options: Ask again later to show the friendship matters
Offer your password in exchange for their password
Ask a mutual friend to persuade them to share
Accept the refusal without further pressure
quizQuestions.answer: Accept the refusal without further pressure
quizQuestions.explanation: Healthy relationships respect consent, privacy, and boundaries without manipulation; accepting a clear no demonstrates trust and protects the other person's autonomy.

quizQuestions.question: What does active listening look and sound like in a conversation?
quizQuestions.answer: Active listening includes giving attention, avoiding interruption, asking clarifying questions, reflecting what was heard, and responding with empathy.
quizQuestions.explanation: A strong response describes observable listening behaviors rather than simply saying to agree with the speaker.

quizQuestions.question: Nicotine in tobacco products affects the developing teen brain by:
options: Acting chiefly on lungs rather than developing brain circuits
Supporting attention without creating a risk of dependence
Disrupting attention, learning, and impulse-control circuits
Causing brief effects that end before learning can be affected
quizQuestions.answer: Disrupting attention, learning, and impulse-control circuits
quizQuestions.explanation: Nicotine is highly addictive and disrupts developing brain circuits responsible for attention, mood regulation, learning, and impulse control in teens.

quizQuestions.question: What is the nationwide minimum legal age to buy alcoholic beverages in the United States?
quizQuestions.explanation: Federal law led every state to use 21 as the minimum age for purchasing alcoholic beverages; this item concerns purchase age, not every state-specific possession exception.

quizQuestions.question: Which is a protective factor that can reduce a teen's risk of substance use?
options: Supportive relationships with trusted adults
Easy access to substances in familiar settings
Peer approval of occasional substance use
Expecting substance use to relieve school stress
quizQuestions.answer: Supportive relationships with trusted adults
quizQuestions.explanation: Trusted adult support is one protective factor; risk and protection reflect multiple interacting influences.

quizQuestions.question: A peer offers a nicotine vape after school. Which response best combines a refusal skill with a protective action?
options: Decline clearly and leave with a supportive friend
Decline softly and stay while the peer keeps offering
Accept the vape and explain that you will not use it
Debate the peer until they agree vaping is risky
quizQuestions.answer: Decline clearly and leave with a supportive friend
quizQuestions.explanation: A clear refusal plus leaving the situation and seeking supportive peers reduces immediate risk.

questions.question: SAMHSA's model identifies how many dimensions of wellness?
questions.explanation: SAMHSA identifies 8 dimensions: emotional, financial, social, spiritual, occupational, physical, intellectual, and environmental.

questions.question: The CDC recommends how many minutes of daily physical activity for teenagers?
options: 60 minutes
90 minutes
30 minutes
20 minutes
questions.answer: 60 minutes
questions.explanation: The CDC recommends at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily for adolescents.

questions.question: Mental health is best described as:
options: Absence of a diagnosed mental-health condition
An ability to stay calm when daily demands increase
Emotional, psychological, and social well-being
High achievement in school and intellectual tasks
questions.answer: Emotional, psychological, and social well-being
questions.explanation: Mental health is a positive concept encompassing emotional, psychological, and social well-being, not just the absence of illness.

questions.question: Which pair represents the rapid sympathetic-adrenal stress response and the slower HPA-axis response, respectively?
options: Melatonin and thyroxine
Estrogen and progesterone
Insulin and glucagon
Epinephrine and cortisol
questions.answer: Epinephrine and cortisol
questions.explanation: Epinephrine (adrenaline) helps mobilize the rapid sympathetic-adrenal response. Cortisol is released through the slower hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) pathway; these are distinct stress-response systems.

questions.question: What sleep range is generally recommended for teenagers each night?
options: 5–6 hours
6–7 hours
11–12 hours
8–10 hours
questions.answer: 8–10 hours
questions.explanation: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine recommends 8–10 hours of sleep per night for teenagers aged 13–18.

questions.question: Blue light from screens disrupts sleep by:
options: Increasing melatonin as the eyes become tired
Suppressing melatonin and delaying sleep timing
Advancing the body clock through mental alertness
Increasing sleep pressure by tiring the brain
questions.answer: Suppressing melatonin and delaying sleep timing
questions.explanation: Bright evening light, including blue light from screens, can suppress melatonin and delay circadian timing. Effects depend on exposure and other habits as well.

questions.question: Which qualities should be present in a healthy relationship?
questions.answer: A healthy relationship is characterized by respect, trust, honest communication, boundaries, support, safety, and shared responsibility.
questions.explanation: The answer should include both positive communication and safety boundaries, because healthy relationships require more than simply spending time together.

questions.question: Which meal best reflects current federal guidance to emphasize nutrient-dense foods?
options: Juice, refined cereal, and a sweetened snack bar
White bread, processed meat, and a sweetened drink
Chips, sweetened yogurt, and a fruit-flavored drink
Vegetables, whole grains, fruit, beans, and water
questions.answer: Vegetables, whole grains, fruit, beans, and water
questions.explanation: Current guidance emphasizes varied nutrient-dense foods and reducing reliance on highly processed foods.

questions.question: Which statement about nicotine exposure from e-cigarettes is most accurate?
options: It can create dependence and disrupt developing brain circuits
Its dependence risk is mainly limited to long-term adult users
Its brain effects are prevented when exposure is infrequent
Its effect on concentration makes it a useful study strategy
questions.answer: It can create dependence and disrupt developing brain circuits
questions.explanation: Nicotine can create dependence and harm developing attention, learning, and impulse-control circuits. Infrequent use does not establish safety, and nicotine is not an appropriate study aid.

questions.question: Which is a warning sign of an unhealthy relationship?
options: Disagreeing while listening to each other’s reasons
Encouraging friendships outside the relationship
Monitoring messages and restricting outside friendships
Asking permission before sharing private information
questions.answer: Monitoring messages and restricting outside friendships
questions.explanation: Controlling, isolating, or monitoring a partner's behavior are red flags for emotional or physical abuse in a relationship.

questions.question: Eustress differs from distress because eustress:
options: Feels manageable and can motivate effort
Lasts longer than other kinds of stress
Describes physical signs rather than emotional reactions
Arises when a person has too few demands to meet
questions.answer: Feels manageable and can motivate effort
questions.explanation: Eustress describes stress experienced as manageable or motivating. Distress feels overwhelming or harmful; the same event can be experienced differently by different people.

questions.question: In a healthy relationship, a personal boundary should be treated as:
options: A starting point for persuading the person to agree
A limit to respect without pressuring the person
A sign that the person has lost trust in the relationship
A temporary preference to revisit whenever refused
questions.answer: A limit to respect without pressuring the person
questions.explanation: Respecting a stated boundary supports trust, safety, and healthy communication; pressure, manipulation, or ignoring the limit undermines each of those qualities.

questions.question: Chronic stress can harm physical health by:
options: Straining stress regulation and heart health
Lowering stress hormones enough to prevent infection
Keeping the immune response steadily more effective
Reducing the body’s need for regular sleep and rest
questions.answer: Straining stress regulation and heart health
questions.explanation: Ongoing stress can disrupt sleep and stress-regulation systems and is associated with immune, cardiovascular, emotional, and cognitive effects.

questions.question: Describe typical REM sleep and how it differs from NREM sleep.
questions.answer: REM usually includes vivid dreaming and muscle atonia. NREM has stages 1–3, including stage 3 deep or slow-wave sleep. Healthy sleep cycles through both phases; recovery is not explained by one stage alone.
questions.explanation: The NHLBI distinguishes three NREM stages from REM. A complete response describes the phases accurately without attributing all recovery to a single stage.

questions.question: Which protective factor can reduce teen substance-use risk?
options: Pressure to meet demanding academic expectations
Lenient expectations with little adult involvement
Supportive family connections and positive peers
Punishment that discourages discussion of mistakes
questions.answer: Supportive family connections and positive peers
questions.explanation: Family connection, caring adults, clear expectations, and positive peer relationships are evidence-supported protective factors that can reduce adolescent substance-use risk.

questions.question: A student improves sleep and then notices better mood and concentration. What wellness principle does this illustrate?
options: Wellness chiefly reflects visible physical changes
Better sleep guarantees improvements in every area
Emotional and intellectual wellness develop separately
Changes in one wellness dimension can affect others
questions.answer: Changes in one wellness dimension can affect others
questions.explanation: Changes in one dimension can influence emotional, intellectual, and physical wellness.

questions.question: Which wellness plan is most likely to be sustainable?
options: Begin many changes together to build motivation quickly
Copy a successful friend’s routine before checking fit
Choose a broad aspiration and leave the schedule open
Choose a few specific changes that fit daily routines
questions.answer: Choose a few specific changes that fit daily routines
questions.explanation: Small, specific, realistic changes are easier to practice, evaluate, and adjust.

questions.question: Which feature most strengthens the credibility of online health information?
options: Qualified authorship, current evidence, and a clear purpose
A detailed personal testimonial with many positive comments
A respected domain name without information about authors
A professional sales page with a polished scientific design
questions.answer: Qualified authorship, current evidence, and a clear purpose
questions.explanation: Credibility depends on authorship, currency, evidence, and transparency; a domain ending alone is not enough.

questions.question: Which statement about preventing nicotine use is most accurate for teenagers?
options: Refusal skills chiefly matter after dependence develops
Avoiding initiation lowers nicotine-dependence risk
Infrequent vaping prevents nicotine from reaching the brain
Nicotine offers a reliable way to improve lasting attention
questions.answer: Avoiding initiation lowers nicotine-dependence risk
questions.explanation: Nicotine can affect the developing brain and create dependence, so prevention and refusal skills matter.

questions.question: A wellness plan is most effective when it does what?
options: Sets realistic steps and reviews progress across dimensions
Chooses ambitious outcomes and postpones progress reviews
Follows a peer’s schedule before checking personal barriers
Prioritizes rapid changes before arranging practical support
questions.answer: Sets realistic steps and reviews progress across dimensions
questions.explanation: A useful wellness plan is realistic, measurable, and balanced across wellness dimensions.

questions.question: How can regular physical activity support more than one dimension of wellness?
questions.answer: Regular activity can support physical health, mood, stress regulation, sleep, social connection, and concentration; a strong response explains at least two linked dimensions.
questions.explanation: The question applies the course's central idea that wellness dimensions interact.

questions.question: A student joins a supportive school club and feels less isolated. Which wellness dimension is most directly strengthened?
options: Social wellness
Environmental wellness
Occupational wellness
Financial wellness
questions.answer: Social wellness
questions.explanation: Supportive relationships and a sense of belonging directly strengthen social wellness and can also influence other dimensions.

questions.question: A student has persistent low mood that is disrupting sleep and schoolwork. Which response best applies the course?
options: Wait until grades decline further before mentioning mood
Ask classmates to manage the problem without adult help
Tell a trusted adult and seek qualified professional help
Use online mood tips instead of discussing ongoing symptoms
questions.answer: Tell a trusted adult and seek qualified professional help
questions.explanation: Symptoms that persist or interfere with daily life deserve support from a trusted adult and qualified professional.

questions.question: Physical inactivity is classified as which type of chronic disease risk factor?
options: A risk marker unrelated to opportunities for activity
A modifiable risk influenced by behavior and access
A clinical diagnosis requiring a single medical test
A fixed inherited risk unaffected by daily routines
questions.answer: A modifiable risk influenced by behavior and access
questions.explanation: Physical activity patterns can often be changed with planning, support, and safer access to activity.

questions.question: Which evening habit best supports healthy sleep?
options: Keep a regular bedtime and reduce bright evening light
Complete work in bed and let fatigue determine bedtime
Use caffeine with dinner to finish homework more quickly
Shift bedtime later during the week and catch up later
questions.answer: Keep a regular bedtime and reduce bright evening light
questions.explanation: A consistent schedule and lower evening light exposure support circadian timing and make adequate sleep more likely.

questions.question: Which listed habit can support sleep quality when practiced consistently?
options: Using caffeine to manage evening tiredness
Using bright screens as part of winding down
Shifting bedtime to match each day’s workload
Keeping similar sleep and wake times all week
questions.answer: Keeping similar sleep and wake times all week
questions.explanation: A regular sleep-wake schedule is an evidence-supported habit that can support sleep timing and quality; it is one part of healthy sleep and not a guaranteed cure for sleep problems.

questions.question: Active listening improves relationships because it:
options: Checks understanding and reduces misunderstandings
Focuses on preparing advice while the person is speaking
Shows agreement before clarifying what the person means
Avoids questions to keep a difficult conversation brief
questions.answer: Checks understanding and reduces misunderstandings
questions.explanation: Active listening — giving full attention and reflecting back what's heard — reduces misunderstandings and strengthens relationship trust.

questions.question: E-cigarettes are harmful to teens because they contain:
questions.answer: E-cigarettes are harmful to teens because many contain nicotine, which is addictive and can harm adolescent brain development; aerosols may also contain other harmful substances.
questions.explanation: A strong answer should not treat vaping as harmless. Nicotine addiction and effects on the developing brain are the central teen-health concerns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes type 2 diabetes risk?
options: Risk is chiefly determined by a single dietary choice
Healthy habits remove inherited susceptibility to disease
Risk has multiple influences, including modifiable ones
Age is a more complete explanation than other influences
questions.answer: Risk has multiple influences, including modifiable ones
questions.explanation: Type 2 diabetes risk has multiple influences; supportive habits and care can lower some risks without guaranteeing an outcome.

questions.question: Which goal most clearly specifies an action, frequency, duration, and review period?
options: Walk more after school when homework becomes manageable
Try a friend’s walking routine without setting a review date
Aim to feel fitter by the next school holiday or break
Walk 20 minutes Mon/Wed/Fri for two weeks, then review
questions.answer: Walk 20 minutes Mon/Wed/Fri for two weeks, then review
questions.explanation: The selected goal states what to do, how long, which days, and for how many weeks. Those details make completion easier to check and the plan easier to review.

questions.question: Occupational wellness in a high school student most directly relates to:
options: Building a broad network of friendships at school
Earning high grades as the main measure of satisfaction
Finding purpose in schoolwork and future work interests
Improving fitness to prepare for demanding daily tasks
questions.answer: Finding purpose in schoolwork and future work interests
questions.explanation: For students, occupational wellness means finding satisfaction, purpose, and engagement in academic work and activities.

questions.question: A student is pressured to try an unknown substance at a party. What is the safest response?
options: Stay nearby and avoid answering the offer directly
Refuse, leave, and contact a trusted support person
Take it to avoid conflict and decide about using it later
Ask the offering peer to judge whether the substance is safe
questions.answer: Refuse, leave, and contact a trusted support person
questions.explanation: A clear refusal, exit plan, and trusted support reduce immediate substance-use risk.

questions.question: Which approach is generally useful for managing different kinds of stress?
options: Use avoidance as the main response to each stressor
Use relaxation before deciding whether any help is needed
Match healthy coping to the stressor and seek needed help
Choose a familiar coping tool regardless of the situation
questions.answer: Match healthy coping to the stressor and seek needed help
questions.explanation: Different stressors call for different evidence-based responses, such as problem solving, activity, relaxation, social support, time management, or professional help when appropriate.

questions.question: Which food choice best supports nutritional wellness?
options: Select meals chiefly by the lowest calorie count
Choose varied nutrient-dense foods and water
Add supplements before evaluating a limited diet
Adjust today’s meals mainly to offset yesterday’s intake
questions.answer: Choose varied nutrient-dense foods and water
questions.explanation: Nutritional wellness emphasizes variety, nutrient density, hydration, and sustainable habits.

questions.question: Tracking progress in a personal wellness plan is important because it:
questions.answer: Tracking progress in a personal wellness plan is important because it shows patterns, measures whether goals are realistic, supports accountability, and helps people adjust habits over time.
questions.explanation: Wellness plans work best when students use evidence from their own behavior to revise goals instead of relying on vague intentions.
